## Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection

**Case:** mta-2024-11-26 | **Analyst source:** PCAP + Suricata/ET alerts (network evidence only)

---

### 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (confirmed via NBNS, mDNS, and Kerberos SPN `host/desktop-b8tqk49.nemotodes.health`) |
| AD domain | nemotodes.health (NetBIOS domain **NEMOTODES**), domain controller **NEMOTODES-DC** at 10.11.26.3 |
| Logged-in user account | **oboomwald** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ `CNameString`, realm NEMOTODES.HEALTH) |

### 2. Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (NetSupport Manager legitimate RAT tooling abused as a remote-access trojan).

Attribution is **signature-confirmed**: ETPRO/ET rules fired directly on the traffic —
- `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`
- `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` / `NetSupport Remote Admin Response`
- `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`

This is corroborated **behaviorally** in the raw pcap: the client's own `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` header, POSTs to `/fakeurl.htm`, and a body prefixed `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<hex blob>` — the known NetSupport client-to-server checkin protocol — repeating on a steady ~60-second beacon interval.

### 3. Infection Chain (observed in traffic, UTC)

1. **04:50:11** — DNS query for `classicgrand.com` (→ 213.246.109.5), TLS session opened. Likely a redirector/landing page in a malvertising or fake-download chain.
2. **04:50:14 – 04:50:40** — Multiple DNS queries and TLS sessions to `modandcrackedapk.com` (→ 193.42.38.139), a "cracked software" themed lure domain, flagged by `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and `...in TLS SNI`. ~5.7 MB is transferred over this TLS session (largest single conversation in the capture), consistent with a payload/installer download inside the encrypted channel.
3. **04:50:45** — Host queries `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (→ 104.26.1.231) and issues `GET /location/loca.asp` — a startup artifact of a freshly launched NetSupport Manager client performing a geolocation lookup.
4. **04:50:45 onward** — Host begins persistent C2 beaconing to **194.180.191.64:443** using plaintext HTTP (mislabeled as port 443, no TLS handshake present) — 58 checkins observed, continuing every ~60 seconds through the end of the capture at **05:43:29 UTC** (~53 minutes of active C2).

Two unrelated SMBv1/NTLMSSP alerts against the DC (10.11.26.3:139/445) and one EFSRPC alert were also present in the Suricata log around 04:49:55–04:50:10; these match ordinary legacy NTLMSSP session-setup/logon behavior toward the domain controller and are not tied to any malicious payload transfer — assessed as noisy/legacy-signature false positives, not part of this compromise.

### 4. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — NetSupport RAT C2, plaintext HTTP POST to `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm`, User-Agent `NetSupport Manager/1.3`

**Malicious/lure domains:**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → 193.42.38.139 — delivery/lure site (fake cracked-software page)
- `classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5 — preceding redirector in the infection chain
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → 104.26.1.231 / 104.26.0.231 / 172.67.68.212 — NetSupport client geolocation service (benign infrastructure abused by the RAT; confirms the client is running)

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` (C2 checkin endpoint)
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` (NetSupport client startup callout)

**Transferred files / hashes:**
None recoverable. The payload delivery to `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139:443) occurred entirely inside TLS, so no filename or file content is visible in cleartext, and no SHA256 can be computed from this capture. All C2 checkin bodies are hex-encoded/obfuscated (`CMD=ENCD` blobs), not raw file data. No HTTP objects with executable/archive content-types were observed anywhere in the capture.

---
**Bottom line:** Workstation DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user `oboomwald` on the NEMOTODES.HEALTH domain, was infected with NetSupport RAT after visiting a fake cracked-software site (`modandcrackedapk.com`, reached via `classicgrand.com`). The malware established persistent C2 to `194.180.191.64:443` and was still actively beaconing at the end of the capture.
